To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glycosylation of prostatic KLK3, 4 or 11 changes the enzymatic activity and the activation profiles of the proteases.
the N-glcans on the prostatic kallikreins 3, 11 and 4 are important for their activity and stability and that their activation by other kallikreens is influenced by their N-glcans.
glycosylated human kallikreins 3, 11, 4, and KLK 2, the activators of KLKs 4 and KLK3/ PSA, were expressed, purified, and characterized in detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the glycosylation pattern and the biological role of N-linked glycans in prostatic kallikreins 3, 11, 3, 2 and 4.
the activation and activity of glyco-KLKs 3,4 and 11, which belong to the prostrate-specific kallikreins.
the activation and activity of human glycosylated kallikreins 3, 11, 4 and KLK2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prostatic group members of the kallikreins are not only upregulated in prostate tumors but also glycosylated.
the glycosylation is important for the activation of pro-KLKs but does not affect their catalytic efficiency.
glycosylation of KLKs is not only important for their secretion, but that it also influences their activation and activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient and robust expression and purification system for human KLKs, which is based on LEXSY and HEK293 systems.
glycosylation of the prostatic KLK proteases is important for their activation and activity.
the N-glycerans of KLKs 4 and KLK11 are essential for efficient activation and activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glycosylation has an important influence on the activation of pro-KLKs and on their enzymatic activity.
N-glycanylated KLKs are more stable and active than the non-glycoslated ones.
the glycosylation status of KLKs has to be taken into account when studying their biological functions.
